articles.title: Troubleshooting Work Email Synchronization
articles.summary: Use this guide when new messages do not appear, outgoing messages remain pending, or your approved email application displays outdated mailbox information. The issue may involve a connection problem, the wrong mailbox, a stuck message, or a synchronization error.

articles.if_not:

- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known email service outage.

articles.title: Improving Slow Computer Performance

4. Remove only unnecessary personal downloads or temporary files that you are authorized to delete.

articles.if_not:
- Save your work, close your applications, and restart the computer through its standard power menu.
- Observe whether the slowdown occurs during video meetings, when opening a particular application, or throughout the workday.
- Record whether the computer freezes repeatedly, overheats, or displays an error.

Avoid downloading third-party cleanup tools or deleting company files to free space.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the computer remains slow after restarting, freezes repeatedly, overheats, or cannot run the applications needed for work. Include when the problem began, which applications are affected, any error messages, and whether the slowdown is constant or intermittent.

articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot hear sound through your speakers or headset, or when other participants cannot hear you during an online meeting. The problem may involve muted controls, an incorrect audio device, a disconnected headset, or application permissions.

5. Review the normal application or browser permissions available to your account and ensure microphone access is allowed.

- Close other applications that may be using the microphone, then reopen the meeting application.
- Disconnect and reconnect the headset, or restart the device after saving your work.
- Check whether the audio problem occurs in multiple applications or only one.

Do not install unofficial audio drivers or change restricted device policies.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the microphone or speakers remain unavailable across multiple applications, your device does not recognize an approved headset, or audio problems affect several employees. articles.title: Troubleshooting a Laptop That Will Not Turn On

- If an approved spare cable or monitor is available, test it to help determine whether the issue involves the cable, monitor, or laptop.
- Record any displayed error, such as a no-signal message, and whether the screen works intermittently.

articles.steps:
1. Save open documents and confirm that important work is backed up to an approved company location.
2. Close applications and browser tabs that you no longer need, particularly those consuming substantial memory.
3. Use the normal storage settings available to your account to check whether the disk is nearly full.
4. Remove only unnecessary personal downloads or temporary files that you are authorized to delete.
5. If performance becomes slow immediately after sign-in, note which applications start automatically. Do not disable security tools or required company software.
6. Follow approved update notifications available to your account, and allow required updates to complete rather than forcing the device to shut down.
articles.if_not:
- Save your work, close your applications, and restart the computer through its standard power menu.
- Observe whether the slowdown occurs during video meetings, when opening a particular application, or throughout the workday.
- Record whether the computer freezes repeatedly, overheats, or displays an error.

Avoid downloading third-party cleanup tools or deleting company files to free space.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the computer remains slow after restarting, freezes repeatedly, overheats, or cannot run the applications needed for work. Include when the problem began, which applications are affected, any error messages, and whether the slowdown is constant or intermittent.

articles.title: Fixing Microphone or Speaker Problems
articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot hear sound through your speakers or headset, or when other participants cannot hear you during an online meeting. The problem may involve muted controls, an incorrect audio device, a disconnected headset, or application permissions.
articles.steps:
1. If you use a wired headset, make sure its cable is securely connected. For wireless equipment, confirm that it is powered on and connected to your device.
2. Increase the speaker volume and verify that the headset, device, and meeting controls are not muted.
3. Open the meeting application's audio settings and select the intended speaker and microphone from the available options.
4. Use the application's built-in speaker and microphone test, if available. Speak normally and check whether the microphone input indicator responds.
5. Review the normal application or browser permissions available to your account and ensure microphone access is allowed.
articles.if_not:
- Close other applications that may be using the microphone, then reopen the meeting application.
- Disconnect and reconnect the headset, or restart the device after saving your work.
- Check whether the audio problem occurs in multiple applications or only one.

Do not install unofficial audio drivers or change restricted device policies.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the microphone or speakers remain unavailable across multiple applications, your device does not recognize an approved headset, or audio problems affect several employees. Include your device type, headset connection type, affected application, and the results of your audio test.

articles.title: Troubleshooting a Laptop That Will Not Turn On
articles.summary: Use this guide when your company laptop does not appear to power on, shows no signs of charging, or displays a blank screen during startup. The device may have no visible response to the power button, or it may start briefly before shutting down.
articles.steps:
1. Confirm that the wall outlet is working by checking it with another suitable device or using another approved outlet.
2. Check that the approved power adapter is firmly connected to the laptop and outlet. Look for obvious damage to the cable or plug.
3. If the battery may be depleted, connect the approved charger and leave the laptop charging for approximately 15 minutes before trying to start it again.
4. Look for power indicators, keyboard lights, or fan activity. If the laptop appears to be running, adjust screen brightness and check whether an external display is masking the issue.
5. Remove nonessential USB devices, docks, and other peripherals, then try starting the laptop with its normal power connection.
articles.if_not:
- If the laptop responds but remains stuck on a screen, follow its approved normal restart procedure.
- Check the IT helpdesk's support guidance using another available device.
- Record whether the device shows indicator lights, charging activity, or other signs of power.

Do not open the laptop casing, remove the internal battery, or attempt electrical repairs.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the device still will not start, the charger or battery appears damaged, or the laptop repeatedly shuts down. Report the device asset number if available, the symptoms, and any visible indicator lights.

articles.title: Troubleshooting an External Monitor With No Display
articles.summary: Use this guide when an external monitor connected to your work laptop displays a blank screen, reports no signal, or is not detected by the computer. The problem may involve monitor power, the selected input source, a loose cable, or display settings.
articles.steps:
1. Confirm that the monitor is switched on and its power cable is securely connected.
2. Use the monitor's normal controls to select the input corresponding to its connected cable.
3. Check that the video cable is securely attached at both ends and look for visible damage.
4. If using an approved docking station or adapter, ensure it is firmly connected to both the laptop and monitor.
5. Open the standard display settings available to your account and check whether the operating system recognizes the second monitor.
6. If the monitor is detected, select the normal extended or duplicated display mode appropriate for your work.
articles.if_not:
- Disconnect and reconnect the display cable, then restart the laptop if necessary.
- If an approved spare cable or monitor is available, test it to help determine whether the issue involves the cable, monitor, or laptop.
- Record any displayed error, such as a no-signal message, and whether the screen works intermittently.

Do not open the monitor casing or install unapproved display drivers.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the monitor remains blank, is not detected, or repeatedly loses its signal after these checks. Include the laptop model, monitor location or asset number, connection type, displayed error, and whether another approved cable or monitor works.

articles.title: Reporting a Suspicious Email
articles.summary: Use this guide when an email appears fraudulent, unexpectedly requests sensitive information, contains a suspicious attachment, or directs you to an unfamiliar sign-in page. Warning signs include mismatched sender details, urgent demands, and requests for passwords or verification codes.
articles.steps:
1. Avoid clicking links, opening attachments, replying, or scanning QR codes included in a suspicious email.
2. Check the sender's full email address and review the message for unusual requests, unexpected payment instructions, or suspicious links.
3. If the email claims to come from a colleague or business contact, verify the request using a known, trusted communication method rather than replying to the suspicious message.
4. If your approved email application provides a phishing-reporting option, use it according to company guidance.
5. Keep the message available for investigation unless company reporting instructions say otherwise. Do not forward it to coworkers or distribute potentially malicious attachments.
articles.if_not:
- Ask the IT helpdesk how to report the message securely if the approved reporting function is unavailable.
- If you clicked a link, opened an attachment, entered credentials, or approved an unexpected authentication request, report that action promptly.
- Preserve relevant message details for investigation without sharing sensitive information unnecessarily.

Do not attempt to investigate a suspicious file yourself or hide a potential security incident.
articles.file_ticket_when: Report the message immediately when it appears suspicious, even if you have not interacted with it. Escalate urgently if you disclosed credentials, downloaded a file, or approved an unexpected sign-in request. Include the message details and actions taken, but never include your password.

articles.title: Troubleshooting VPN Connection Failures
articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot establish a company VPN connection while working remotely or when an existing connection disconnects unexpectedly. Symptoms may include connection timeouts, repeated failures, or inaccessible company resources even when the VPN appears connected.
articles.steps:
1. Open a familiar public website to confirm that your home or other approved network has a working internet connection.
2. Check the company's published remote-work instructions to determine whether the VPN is required for the resource you are accessing.
3. Disconnect from the VPN, wait a few seconds, and reconnect using the approved VPN application and sign-in method.
articles.if_not:
- Confirm that you are using your current work account and that your password has not expired. Never share your password with support personnel.
- Save your work, restart your laptop, and attempt another VPN connection.
- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known VPN outage.

Do not disable security software, install another VPN application, or change company network settings to bypass the connection problem.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the VPN continues to fail, your account is rejected despite correct credentials, or several remote employees experience the same issue. Include the error message, approximate time of failure, whether your regular internet connection works, and whether the problem started after a password change.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Wi-Fi Connection Issues
articles.summary: Use this guide when your computer cannot connect to the company Wi-Fi, repeatedly disconnects, or reports that it is connected without internet access. The network may be missing from the available networks list, or the wireless signal may be weak.
articles.steps:
1. Make sure Wi-Fi is enabled on your device and airplane mode is turned off.
2. Move closer to the office wireless access point or to an area where the Wi-Fi signal is stronger.
3. Disconnect from the company Wi-Fi, wait a few seconds, and reconnect using your usual approved access method.
4. Check whether another approved device can connect to the same network to help determine whether the problem affects one device or multiple users.
articles.if_not:
- Save your work, restart your computer, and try connecting again.
- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known network outage.
- Note whether the company Wi-Fi network is missing entirely or appears but fails to connect.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if you still cannot connect after these checks, if the company Wi-Fi remains unavailable on your device, or if multiple employees are affected. Include your work location, device type, the time the issue began, and any displayed error messages.

articles.title: Resolving Shared Folder Access Problems
articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot open a shared company folder or document that you normally use for work. You may see an access-denied message, find that a shared location is missing, or discover that a previously available file is no longer accessible.
articles.steps:
1. Verify that you are signed in with your assigned work account rather than a personal or secondary account.
2. Confirm that you are using the correct shared location or approved shortcut. Check the original link or instructions supplied by your team.
3. If the shared folder requires the office network or VPN, verify that you are connected through the approved method.
4. Navigate to the shared folder through the company's standard file system or approved document portal instead of an old bookmark.
5. Determine whether the problem affects one file, one folder, or several shared locations.
6. If appropriate, ask a teammate who is authorized to use the same folder whether they can access it.
articles.if_not:
- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known shared-storage outage.
- Record the folder location and exact error message without copying sensitive document contents into an unrelated request.
- Check the company's approved access instructions for the affected shared location.

Do not attempt to change folder permissions, use another employee's account, or move restricted files to a personal storage service.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if access remains denied, a previously available folder disappears, or you need authorization for a new folder. Include the folder path or approved link, the business reason for access, the error message, and whether teammates are affected.

articles.summary: Use this guide when your company laptop does not appear to power on, shows no signs of charging, or displays a blank screen during startup. The device may have no visible response to the power button, or it may start briefly before shutting down.
articles.steps:

5. Open the standard display settings available to your account and check whether the operating system recognizes the second monitor.
6. If the monitor is detected, select the normal extended or duplicated display mode appropriate for your work.

- Disconnect and reconnect the display cable, then restart the laptop if necessary.
- If an approved spare cable or monitor is available, test it to help determine whether the issue involves the cable, monitor, or laptop.
- Record any displayed error, such as a no-signal message, and whether the screen works intermittently.

articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the monitor remains blank, is not detected, or repeatedly loses its signal after these checks. Include the laptop model, monitor location or asset number, connection type, displayed error, and whether another approved cable or monitor works.

articles.title: Troubleshooting VPN Connection Failures
articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot establish a company VPN connection while working remotely or when an existing connection disconnects unexpectedly. Symptoms may include connection timeouts, repeated failures, or inaccessible company resources even when the VPN appears connected.
articles.steps:
1. Open a familiar public website to confirm that your home or other approved network has a working internet connection.
2. Check the company's published remote-work instructions to determine whether the VPN is required for the resource you are accessing.
3. Disconnect from the VPN, wait a few seconds, and reconnect using the approved VPN application and sign-in method.
articles.if_not:

articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if the VPN continues to fail, your account is rejected despite correct credentials, or several remote employees experience the same issue. Include the error message, approximate time of failure, whether your regular internet connection works, and whether the problem started after a password change.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Wi-Fi Connection Issues
articles.summary: Use this guide when your computer cannot connect to the company Wi-Fi, repeatedly disconnects, or reports that it is connected without internet access. The network may be missing from the available networks list, or the wireless signal may be weak.
articles.steps:
1. Make sure Wi-Fi is enabled on your device and airplane mode is turned off.
2. Move closer to the office wireless access point or to an area where the Wi-Fi signal is stronger.
3. Disconnect from the company Wi-Fi, wait a few seconds, and reconnect using your usual approved access method.
4. Check whether another approved device can connect to the same network to help determine whether the problem affects one device or multiple users.
articles.if_not:
- Save your work, restart your computer, and try connecting again.
- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known network outage.
- Note whether the company Wi-Fi network is missing entirely or appears but fails to connect.

articles.title: Resolving Shared Folder Access Problems
articles.summary: Use this guide when you cannot open a shared company folder or document that you normally use for work. You may see an access-denied message, find that a shared location is missing, or discover that a previously available file is no longer accessible.
articles.steps:
1. Verify that you are signed in with your assigned work account rather than a personal or secondary account.
2. Confirm that you are using the correct shared location or approved shortcut. Check the original link or instructions supplied by your team.
3. If the shared folder requires the office network or VPN, verify that you are connected through the approved method.
4. Navigate to the shared folder through the company's standard file system or approved document portal instead of an old bookmark.
5. Determine whether the problem affects one file, one folder, or several shared locations.
6. If appropriate, ask a teammate who is authorized to use the same folder whether they can access it.
articles.if_not:
- Ask the IT helpdesk whether there is a known shared-storage outage.
- Record the folder location and exact error message without copying sensitive document contents into an unrelated request.
- Check the company's approved access instructions for the affected shared location.

Do not attempt to change folder permissions, use another employee's account, or move restricted files to a personal storage service.
articles.file_ticket_when: File a ticket if access remains denied, a previously available folder disappears, or you need authorization for a new folder. Include the folder path or approved link, the business reason for access, the error message, and whether teammates are affected.
